products.title: Aeropress XL
products.body_html:
Our iconic coffee press, made with the same patented technology, now with double the capacity. Includes a 20 oz carafe (30 eur value) made of crystal-clear shatterproof Tritan™.

3-in-1 brew technology combines the best of several brew methods into one easy to use, very portable device. No more average joe from fancy, expensive machines. Smooth, rich, grit-free coffee with a delicious, full-bodied finish that lingers well after your last sip.

Compact, durable and lightweight so you can pack it in your bag and take it on the road. No more mediocre (at best) coffee from the hotel, office, Airbnb, ski lodge, camper…

The world's best kept coffee secret – 55K+ five star reviews in over 60 countries.

AeroPress uses a patented 3 in 1 brew technology that combines the flavor benefits of espresso, pour-over and french press into one compact, portable device. You get a completely unique and delicious cup of coffee, only possible with an AeroPress

First, water is poured over the coffee, wetting and aerating the grinds, creating the signature AeroPress smoothness. Then, during the immersion process, water penetrates the coffee grinds for deeper flavor notes and a full bodied finish often found in a French Press. Finally, the magic happens - air pressure quickly pushes the brew through the coffee bed and filter, removing grit and bitter tasting oils for an espresso-like richness

products.title: Balaycho — Yirgacheffe Ethiopia
products.body_html:
From the lush highlands of Sidamo, this naturally processed Ethiopian lot captures the essence of one of coffee’s most iconic origins. Grown between 1,500 and 3,000 meters, the cherries flourish in fertile volcanic soil and cool mountain air, producing a cup that is both vivid and complex.

Sourced through Mecota Trading, a collective that empowers smallholder farmers while preserving traceability and craft, this coffee showcases local landrace varieties — a living expression of Ethiopia’s genetic coffee heritage.

In the cup, expect an expressive profile of blackberry, floral tones, brown sugar, and caramelized orange, with a wild and layered complexity that lingers long after each sip.

Roasted by SOLO Lisboa, awarded Best Roastery in Portugal 2025 (jury & public choice) at Porto Coffee Week, and recognized for Sustainability at the My Coffee Awards in Barcelona.
Crafted under the vision of Dani Cassiano, one of the winners of Coffee Personality of the Year 2025.

A celebration of origin, artistry, and conscious roasting — from Ethiopia to your cup.

Country: Ethiopia
Region: Sidamo
Producer: Mecota Trading
Variety: Local landraces
Process: Natural

products.title: Cafec Abaca Trapezoid Paper Filter 103
products.body_html:
CAFEC Abaca Trapezoid Paper Filter – Size 103

Looking for a more sustainable way to brew delicious coffee? The CAFEC Abaca Trapezoid Paper Filters are just what you need. Made from a natural blend of abaca (also known as Manila hemp) and wood pulp, these eco-friendly filters are both strong and gentle on the environment.

Approved by the Japan Hand Drip Championship (JHDC), these filters are known for producing high-quality coffee with bright, clean acidity.

Why choose Abaca paper filters?
Unlike regular paper filters, CAFEC’s Abaca filters feature a unique double crepe design. This creates a thin air layer between the filter and your dripper, allowing for ideal water flow and extraction.

What makes the CAFEC Abaca 103 filters so great?

  • Made with abaca fiber — 4x stronger than regular wood pulp
  • 100% natural and unbleached
  • Excellent water permeability for an even extraction
  • Size 103 – perfect for 5 to 7 cups

Compatible with:
Clever Dripper 500ml, Fellow Aiden, Kalita 103, Melitta #4, Bee House Dripper, Bonavita Dripper, Moccamaster, Sage Precision Brew, Wilfa Svart Presisjon

Key Benefits:

products.title: Cafetto EVO Espresso Machine Cleaner 500g
products.body_html:
With its rapidly soluble and free-rinsing formulation, EVO® removes coffee oils, grounds and stains, improving the taste and aroma of espresso.

Ingredients are rapidly biodegradable and odorless.

Non-GMO and free from phosphates and chlorine.

Non-corrosive formulation to protect the machine.

A measuring scoop is included in 1kg and 500g jars for accurate dosing.


Directions

PROCEDURE TO BACKFLUSH EACH DELIVERY GROUP

  1. Remove coffee filter from group handle, and replace with blind filter.
  2. For daily cleaning add 1 level scoop of EVO® into the group handle and insert as if brewing espresso. If the machine is cleaned less often, use 2 level scoops.
  3. Start cycle and allow to run for 10 seconds to dissolve cleaner.
  4. Stop cycle and allow to sit for 10 seconds.
  5. Start and stop cycle 4 more times - run for 10 seconds, stop for 10 seconds.
  6. Remove the group handle and rinse well under stream of water from delivery group. Turn off.
  7. Re-insert handle with blind filter, start and stop cycle 10 times - run for 5 seconds, stop for 2 seconds to ensure thorough rinsing.
  8. Remove blind filter and insert regular filter.
  9. Brew and discard a single espresso to re-season machine.

PROCEDURE TO CLEAN FILTERS AND GROUP HANDLES

  1. Soak group handles and filters in 500mL of hot water with 2 level scoops of EVO® Espresso Machine Cleaner for 10 minutes.
  2. Rinse thoroughly in running hot water.

Recommended For

Traditional espresso machines.

products.title: Cafetto GC2 Grinder Cleaner 450g
products.body_html:
Coffee Grinder Cleaner

100% Natural
Cafetto® GC2 is a natural seed-based proprietary formula that does not contain any binders or chemicals during processing.

Safe for your machine
The ingredients feed through the grinder burrs/blades easily, with no clogging or damage. Safely removes build-up of stale coffee and coffee odours.

No grinder disassembly required
Simply use GC2 through the grinder for exceptional results without the need to take the grinder apart.

Why clean Grinders regularly?
Cleaning the internal components of a coffee grinder are often overlooked or deemed unnecessary. However, cleaning the internals will remove build up of stale coffee residue, odours and reduce blockages between burrs and chutes. Cleaning will also improve grinder performance and extend the working life of its burrs.

Does GC2 damage the grinder burrs? We have modelled GC2 to the hardness similar to a roasted coffee bean. Therefore this can be extrapolated to have similar long term effects on the coffee burrs.

GC2 contains gluten and should not be used in coffee grinder systems for gluten intolerant persons.

Directions

  1. Pour one capful of Cafetto® GC2 into hopper.
  2. Run grinder to grind all Grinder Clean in hopper.
  3. Empty the grinder dosing chamber and brush out any dust with Pallo Grind Minder.
  4. To season burrs, repeat above process once with one capful of coffee beans.


Recommended For

Cleaning grinder burrs and casings. Use Cafetto® Barista Wipes to keep the outside of your Grinder Hopper clean. For a gluten free option, Cafetto recommend to use Grinder Clean.

Brazil, shaped by origin and consistency.

This is a grounded expression of Brazilian specialty coffee from the Cerrado Mineiro, produced by D Barbosa at Fazenda Sucurí. A coffee that reflects the strength of a certified origin, combining traceability, environmental responsibility and a profile built on balance and reliability.

From harvest to drying, every step follows a precise rhythm. Cherries are carefully selected and dried on cement patios for 11 days, allowing sugars to concentrate and structure to develop. The result is a consistent and well-defined cup, shaped by both process and terroir.

In the cup, this coffee is comforting and structured, with a classic Brazilian profile. Notes of chocolate lead the experience, supported by a deep sweetness and full body. The low acidity keeps the profile smooth and accessible, delivering a balanced and satisfying cup.

This lot is part of the Região do Cerrado Mineiro certification and carries the Rainforest Alliance seal, reinforcing a commitment to quality, traceability and responsible production.

products.title: Cascara Burundi Migoti 100g Infusion Coffee
products.body_html:
A New Way to Experience Coffee!

Ever wondered what coffee tastes like beyond the bean? Our SOLO Burundi Cascara offers a unique and refreshing experience, made from the dried coffee cherry husk. Naturally sweet and fruity, this cascara brews into a vibrant infusion, perfect for those looking to explore coffee in a whole new way.

How It’s Made

The cascara is prepared with care and simplicity. After coffee cherries are depulped, the skins are collected and placed on raised beds to dry. Once they reach 10-12% moisture, they are carefully bagged and stored, preserving their rich aromas and delicate flavors.

How to Brew

Brewing cascara is easy and rewarding! Here’s our recommended recipe:
🔸 6g of cascara
🔸 200ml of water at 93°C

1️⃣ Rinse the cascara with hot water (93°C) to enhance the flavors.
2️⃣ Add the full 200ml of hot water and let it steep for 3 minutes.
3️⃣ Strain and enjoy your naturally sweet, fruity infusion!

👉 SOLO Tip: For the best extraction, we recommend using the HARIO Largo 35 Tea Dripper Server Set TDR-5012, available in our webshop. It ensures an even, flavorful infusion—bringing out the best in your cascara!

Discover the fruity side of coffee with SOLO Burundi Cascara. Try it now!

products.title: Cherry Bomb cofermented natural by Solo Brewing
products.body_html:
Cherry Bomb – A Co-fermented Natural by SOLO Brewing

Some coffees arrive with a story. Cherry Bomb arrives with an explosion. Born from the creative minds at El Vergel Estate in Tolima, Colombia, this co-fermented natural is the result of years of innovation, community, and an obsession with pushing the boundaries of what coffee can taste like. Crafted from Castillo and Colombia varietals sourced from a network of 250 coffee-growing families across Tolima, Huila, and Caldas, this is a coffee that carries the spirit of an entire region in every sip.

The result in the cup is bold, expressive, and unforgettable. Expect an intense wave of ripe cherry and ginja, layered with dark chocolate richness, warm spices, and a sweetness that lingers long after the last drop. This is specialty coffee at its most adventurous — and most delicious.

Process Information

The journey of Cherry Bomb begins with the careful handpicking of Castillo and Colombia coffee cherries from farms across Tolima, Huila, and Caldas. Once selected, the cherries are transported to El Vergel Estate, where they undergo rigorous hand-sorting to ensure optimal ripeness and freshness. The coffee then enters a 48-hour anaerobic pre-fermentation in sealed plastic bags, activating enzymatic reactions that lay the foundation for structured flavor development.

Following pre-fermentation, the coffee moves into a co-fermentation stage with yeasts and red cherry flavors, intentionally designed to amplify its fruit-forward profile. Sugarcane is added to increase available sugar content, extending the fermentation to five days for greater depth and complexity. Once complete, the coffee is pre-dried under direct sunlight on raised beds before transferring to static mechanical silos for controlled drying. A final 30-day stabilization period allows the flavors to fully harmonize and mature before export.

Why this coffee matters

  • Co-fermented with red cherry and sugarcane for an explosive, fruit-forward profile
  • Sourced from 250 coffee-growing families across Tolima, Huila, and Caldas
  • Processed at the pioneering El Vergel Estate, founded by Martha, Shady, and Elias
  • A testament to innovation and community in Colombian specialty coffee since 2019
  • Roasted with precision by SOLO Brewing Lisbon

Cherry Bomb is a limited release for those who dare to experience coffee at its most expressive. A co-fermented natural that detonates with flavor — and leaves you wanting more.

The Label – A Tribute to Our People

The Cherry Bomb can is more than packaging — it is a love letter. Inspired by the iconic crowd illustration on Green Day’s Dookie album cover, the label is a hand-illustrated tribute to the friends, partners, and people who have been part of the SOLO Brewing journey. Every face on this can belongs to someone who has left a mark on our story — people who passed through our lives, shared a cup, believed in what we were building, or simply made the ride more meaningful.

We tried to fit as many of our people as we could. If you spot yourself — or someone you know — on this can, we’d love to hear from you. Leave a comment below and tell us your story with SOLO Brewing. 🍒

Country: Colombia
Farm: Processed at El Vergel Estate
Producer: Producers from Tolima, Huila & Caldas – Forest Coffee
Region: Huila, Tolima, Caldas
Varietal: Castillo, Colombia
Altitude: 1,750 MASL
Process: Natural + Red Cherry Co-fermentation
Sensory Notes: Cherry, Chocolate, Ginja, Spices

products.title: DESCALMA – SOLO Drip Coffee Brew Bag
products.body_html:
Coffee without limits.

Take specialty coffee anywhere with our new SOLO Brewing drip bags. Each individual sachet contains 13g of freshly ground coffee, perfectly dosed for one cup. Ideal for travelers, busy mornings, or that special pause in your day, DESCALMA brings you the quality of our roasting in a practical, single-serve format. Just add hot water and enjoy. No equipment needed.

A new way to enjoy SOLO’s signature roast

DESCALMA is the “practical cousin” of our beloved CALMA, but with caffeine. Infused with passion fruit pulp, it shares the same tropical vibe, designed for coffee lovers who don’t want to compromise on flavor, even on the go. Slip a few drip bags into your bag or backpack and always have a special coffee moment within reach.

How it works
Just like a tea bag:

  1. Place the drip bag in your cup.
  2. Pour 240 ml of hot water (95ºC).
  3. Dunk it 4 or 5 times.
  4. Let it steep for 5 minutes.
  5. Remove, sip, and enjoy.

    Each sachet = one perfect cup.

About the Producer

Finca Monteblanco is a 14-hectare family-run farm located in the San Adolfo region of Huila, Colombia, managed by Rodrigo Sánchez Valencia alongside his wife Claudia Samboni, their daughter Nathalia, and farm manager Don Gerardo. Nestled beside the Cueva de los Guácharos National Natural Park and the Suaza River Valley, the farm benefits from rich biodiversity and ideal environmental conditions.

Monteblanco is renowned for its dedication to producing exceptional coffees, cultivating varieties such as Geisha, Pink Bourbon, Pacamara, and Purple Caturra. Since 2017, Rodrigo has united six family farms under Aromas del Sur, which also includes their own dry mill in Pitalito.


Tropical Fermentation Process

The Tropical process begins by creating a mother culture: microorganisms are isolated and added to a mix of pineapple, passion fruit, orange, and mango. Fed with panela and sugar, this culture grows in sweetness and complexity before being used in the coffee fermentation.

Once harvested, cherries are pulped and placed in 200-liter sealed tanks with the culture for 150 hours. Carefully monitored Brix and pH levels ensure the fruit flavors shine through without overpowering the coffee’s natural character. The result? A vibrant cup with bright tropical notes, balanced body, and remarkable drinkability.


COUNTRY: Colombia

REGION: San Adolfo, Huila

PRODUCER: Rodrigo Sánchez Valencia & family

FARM: Finca Monteblanco

VARIETAL: Blend of co-fermented varieties (including Pink Bourbon, Purple Caturra)

ALTITUDE: 1,730 MASL

PROCESS: Tropical Co-fermentation (pineapple, passion fruit, orange, mango)

FLAVOR NOTES: Passion Fruit, Fermented, Caramelized

FORMAT: Individual drip sachet, 13g of ground coffee


Why DESCALMA?

✔ Specialty coffee roasted by SOLO Brewing Lisboa
✔ Infused with tropical vibrancy from passion fruit co-fermentation
✔ Pre-dosed 13g sachets – one cup of specialty coffee anytime, anywhere
✔ Perfect for home, work, travel, or your Airbnb stay in Portugal

products.title: Geisha AB – Leon Christianakys
products.body_html:
Acacia Hills Geisha AB – New Harvest by SOLO Brewing

This coffee carries a special story in the history of SOLO Brewing. In 2024, the previous harvest of this Geisha was selected after a highly competitive selection among Portuguese roasteries and chosen as the official coffee of the Portuguese Aeropress Championship. For a young roastery, this recognition was an honor and a milestone, proving the quality of our sourcing and roasting.

We are now proud to release the new harvest of this remarkable Geisha from Acacia Hills, Tanzania. Unlike the previous AA lot, this release comes from the Geisha AB variety, offering a unique expression of the terroir while preserving the clarity and elegance that made it stand out. Expect layers of delicate sweetness reminiscent of waffles, floral notes of orange blossom, and juicy peach flavors, all wrapped in a silky body with a lingering smooth finish.

Process Information

The cherries are carefully sorted in the field and at the washing station before de-pulping in the evening. The coffee undergoes open fermentation for 12 to 13 hours, with close monitoring to ensure balance and precision. After fermentation, the beans are washed and graded into P1, P2, and floaters. Drying takes place over 13 to 16 days, depending on weather conditions, until the parchment reaches a moisture content of 12 percent. Finally, the coffee is moved to a dry storage area to preserve its integrity before export.


Why this coffee matters

  • Official coffee of the Portuguese Aeropress Championship 2024
  • New harvest of the celebrated Geisha from Acacia Hills, Tanzania
  • Now available in the AB variety, showcasing a fresh and distinctive profile
  • Roasted with precision by SOLO Brewing Lisbon

This is a limited release for those who seek exceptional specialty coffee, with a proven track record on the competition stage and a new expression that highlights the complexity and elegance of the Geisha variety.

Country: Tanzania
Farm: Acacia Hills
Varietal: Geisha AB
Altitude: 1.750-1.950 MASL
Process: Fully Washed
Sensory Notes: Waffles, Vanilla, Light peach and orange flowers

products.title: Geisha ZEO Colombia Diego Bermudez
products.body_html:
Exclusive PRE-SALE

Only 20 units will be made!

It will be roasted on 16/12/24 with expected shipping on 17/12/24

60 grams of the most esquisite coffee we ever tried!

The Geisha Zeo, from zeolites , is a experiment from Diego Bermudez, and we where blessed to have our hands on it! Only 3kg of green beans where avaiable, and we made a 1,2kgs for the public, and the rest is to be tasted in our coffeeshop with a specific Apax recipe using Sibarist Papers.

This process delivers a coffee like no other, with almost zero fermentation! Do not miss this once in a lifetime oportunity to have at home these amazing beans or gift a loved one with this amazing experience!

Producer: Diego Bermudez

Origin: Colombia

Finca El Paraiso

Altitute: 1960m

Variety: Geisha

Process: Experimental with Zeolites

Profile: Sweet geisha Fruit, jasmine, lemongrass, apricot

From the Producer:

As close to zero fermentation as possible, Zeo offers a profile that tastes like no coffee you've tasted before but exactly like coffee should.


Zeo is the latest innovation from a team redefining the world of coffee processing. In every process, fermentation is both necessary and inevitable. Diego Bermudez and Finca El Paraíso however have developed a technique to remove seed from cherry with virtually no fermentation at all. The goal: to present a geisha in it's purest form, as a cup with the closest possible expression to its fruit.


To start El Paraíso cultivate the best geisha possible by selectively growing the seedlings for this lot. To capture the clean, complex, and floral qualities the varietal is prized for takes a few careful steps.


Cherries of optimal ripeness are hand-picked, immersed in an ozone bath to remove impurities and microbes and then frozen at -40°C in 4hrs. The frozen fruit is moved to a vacuum drying chamber where a combination of zeolites (a compound with a high absorption rate) and negative pressure rapidly dehydrate the coffee cherries and preserves the Geisha's natural structure, colour, and flavour. The result is a no-fermentation coffee that's never been heated and has the dehydrated pulp still intact.
A process that takes less than 10hrs from harvest, delivers an experience of the rarity of geisha in its truest form – as a fruit.


Expect a cup with a light body, beautiful progressive stone fruit acidity, round sweetness, with notes of jasmine, lemongrass, apricot, and litchi (very much like biting into the fruit of a geisha cherry )

products.title: Piña Colada Purple Caturra Coffee
products.body_html:
From the mountains of Huila, Rodrigo Sanchez Valencia at Finca Monteblanco, created this amazing process that infused this coffee with an indistigued aroma of a Pina Colada!

Fresh Roasted in our coffeeshop, this amazing beans will bring the summer back!

COUNTRY: COLOMBIA, HUILA

FARM: MONTEBLANCO

VARIETAL: PURPLE CATURRA

ALTITUDE : 1.730 masl

PROCESS : CO-FERMENTED WITH COCONUT AND LEMONADE 

SENSORY NOTES : PINA COLADA, LEMONADE, RUM, COCONUT

 

FROM THE PRODUCER:

Finca Monteblanco is located near Cueva de los Guacharos, one of the 59 protected parks in Colombia. The Suaza river also runs nearby and provides fresh water for cultivation and processing.

Rodrigo cultivates Caturra, Geisha, Pink Bourbon and Pacamara varieties on Finca Monteblanco. The high altitude and superb microclimate of Acevedo, Huila creates the ideal conditions for cultivating specialty coffees..

Cherry is selectively handpicked and delivered to the on-site wet mill. Rodrigo selected “Purple Caturra” for this lot, a Caturra variety with different leaves and cherry color than Red Caturra. When measured on Brix sugar content meters, “purple” Caturra has higher Brix content than typical Red Caturra. Cherry is floated to remove any under or over-ripe coffee.

Before processing cherry, Rodrigo combines a mixture of lactobacillus, saccharomyses and cerevisiae bacteria for a total of 10 different yeasts to cherry to promote fermentation. Rodrigo also added cholupa, a sour fruit often used to make a form of lemonade, and dried coconut to this mixture to add additional flavor. Finally, he adds a sugar-rich mixture to feed fermentation, such as molasses, panela or granulated sugar. The mixture is sealed and fermented for 8 days. After 8 days, cherry is added to the fruit mixture and fermented for 180 hours (7.5 days).

Following fermentation, coffee is washed in clean water and laid in parabolic beds to dry. Cherry is raked frequently to ensure even drying. It takes approximately 25 to 30 days for cherry to dry.

products.title: Sibarist Fast Cone Paper M 100pcs
products.body_html:
CONE FAST Specialty Coffee Filter

The fastest filter on the market. Reinvent your recipes, reach new cups and rediscover your coffees.

FAST Specialty Coffee Filter technology is a unique fibre composition that provides an unprecedented “drawdown” circulation of liquid (dissolution of soluble coffee particles) through its structure, offering a fast, constant flow in extractions while retaining the solid, non-soluble particles. This results in a clean, silky cup, free of external flavours.

FAST filters open up a new world of preparation possibilities, giving the barista the chance to experiment and obtain formerly limited features such as: faster flows, elimination of the need for air channels, increased extraction and heat delivery performance… These are some of the features offered by the FAST line.

The SIBARIST purpose

Was to create a very unique filter from all the existing coffee filters, with an outstanding flow rate and drawdown using the best possible materials, with the same care for coffee, produced in Barcelona.

Why a filtration technology?

In our desire to succeed in extracting the best of each coffee, we constantly adjust and juggle all the variables of the extraction, striving to obtain the best possible cup. But there is one element of the infusion that is not a variable: it is a constant. We cannot modify its properties; we subconsciously adapt all the variables of the recipe to its retention capacity (permeability), restricting all the other variables to this factor and adjusting to it.

Focus on quality above quantity

Developing a tool to allow the coffee community to reinvent their recipes, achieving new and different cup profiles and rediscovering coffees, facilitates experimentation in the search for the best possible extraction.

We seek the best quality, devoting the same care to the filter as to getting an exceptional cup of coffee. We pay attention to detail throughout the whole chain, from the origin of the raw material on estates and plantations to its local processing and manufacture. We reflect the values and standards that characterise specialty. We focus on quality above quantity. This is a product with a history similar to that of a coffee bean. Its whole process is reflected in the cup, in the form of possibilities, irregularities, aromas and flavours. We have to measure up.

SIBARIST BRAND PHILOSOPHY

The FLAT & CONE FAST Specialty Coffee Filters are entirely produced locally in Barcelona.

products.title: Sunset Chocolate DECAF - Red & Yellow Caturra, Colombia (Harvest 2026)
products.body_html:
Sunset Chocolate Decaf – Red & Yellow Caturra, Colombia

From the volcanic soils of Tolima, Colombia, Sunset Chocolate Decaf is our sweet escape from the idea that decaf is dull. From the 2026 harvest, this coffee is grown at 1,450 MASL on the forward-thinking El Vergel Estate. This 100% Arabica blend of Red and Yellow Caturra is naturally decaffeinated using Colombian sugarcane, keeping all the flavor and none of the buzz.

El Vergel is led by the visionary Bayter family, Elías and Shady, who transformed their avocado farm into one of Colombia’s most innovative coffee projects. With decades of dedication and experimentation, they're redefining what decaf can be.

🧪 Precision fermentation meets smooth decaf
These cherries undergo a 48–60 hour anaerobic fermentation to develop their juicy, tropical profile. After sun-drying and mechanical drying at low temperatures, they’re gently decaffeinated using the Sugarcane EA method, a natural process that preserves complexity without compromising quality.

☕ Flavor profile
Sunset Chocolate is a smooth, comforting cup with a rich, dessert-like character. Expect notes of milk chocolate, almond, molasses, and a gentle touch of clove, creating a warm, balanced profile that’s beautifully layered and clean. Perfect hot or over ice.

🌱 Naturally decaffeinated in Colombia
Using ethyl acetate derived from local sugarcane, this method keeps things natural and delicious. You’d never know it’s decaf, and that’s the point.

Origins & Process:

Variety: Red & Yellow Caturra
Producer: Elías & Shady Bayter
Farm: El Vergel Estate – Fresno, Tolima, Colombia
Harvest: 2026
Altitude: 1,450 m.a.s.l.
Process: Natural Anaerobic
Fermentation: 48–60h anaerobic
Drying: Raised beds & mechanical (below 45ºC)
Decaffeination: Sugarcane EA (Ethyl Acetate)
Stabilization: 45 days in GrainPro bags

Milk Chocolate
Almond
Molasses
Clove

Born at El Vergel Estate in Tolima, Colombia, this co-fermented natural is the result of years of innovation and an obsession with pushing the limits of what coffee can taste like. Sourced from 250 coffee-growing families across Tolima, Huila, and Caldas, the cherries undergo 48 hours of anaerobic pre-fermentation before entering a five-day co-fermentation with red cherry and sugarcane — a process designed to amplify depth, sweetness, and complexity in ways that are impossible to forget.

products.body_html:
⚠️ Pre-order — Ships Mid-September 2026. Roasted to order and shipped from mid-September 2026 to ensure the coffee is properly rested before the global cupping event on 3rd October. Only 280 kits available worldwide.

🎁 Want the full SOLO Brewing fermentation experience?

We've brought together this kit alongside our most iconic fermented releases — Cherry Bomb, Hop Hour, and Metacafeína — into one unmissable limited bundle.

⚠️ Strictly limited. Only 60 bundles available worldwide.

→ GET THE FULL FERMENTATION PROJECT BUNDLE ←

The Fermentation Project — by James Hoffmann

When James Hoffmann announced The Fermentation Project, we didn't hesitate for a second.

The Fermentation Project is a global initiative created by James Hoffmann — one of the most respected voices in specialty coffee — to explore, document, and celebrate the science of fermentation in coffee processing. The project brings together roasters from around the world, all working with the same sourced coffees, to participate in a global cupping event on 3rd October 2026. The goal: to understand how roasting approach, geography, and preparation affect the same fermented lots — and to share those findings with the wider coffee community.

All four coffees in this kit are sourced directly through The Fermentation Project. James Hoffmann and his team selected and curated these lots to represent four distinct points on the fermentation spectrum — from a classic washed to the most extreme end of controlled fermentation science.

🎥 Watch James Hoffmann introduce The Fermentation Project →

Learn more at thefermentationproject.com.

Why We Jumped at This

At SOLO Brewing, fermentation has never been a gimmick. Since we first lit the roaster in Lisbon, we have been obsessed with processed coffees — the ones that push boundaries, that carry the fingerprint of a producer's obsession, that taste like nothing else in the cup. You may already know our fermented releases: HOP HOUR, co-fermented with IPA yeast, CHERRY BOMB, born from five days of red cherry co-fermentation at El Vergel Estate in Colombia, and METACAFEÍNA — Castillo 720 by Diego Bermudez, fermented 720 hours with lactobacillus and finished with thermal shock — one of the most extreme and celebrated fermented coffees in the world.

When James Hoffmann built a project around exactly this philosophy and invited roasters who share this passion to participate, it felt like a natural home for us. We are proud to be part of it — and even prouder to bring it to you.

The Four Coffees — A Study in Fermentation

Each of the four lots in this kit represents a distinct approach to fermentation — designed to be tasted side by side, and to answer a single question: what does fermentation actually do to coffee?

☕ 01 — Washed · The Baseline

A classically processed washed coffee — clean, transparent, and free of fermentation influence. The reference point against which every other coffee in this kit is measured.

Process: Fully washed · Character: Clean, bright, terroir-driven

✨ Love clean, terroir-driven washed coffees? Try Geisha AB — Leon Christianakys — a pristine washed Geisha that lets the variety and origin speak without interference.

🌿 02 — Wild Yeast Fermentation · Spontaneous & Unpredictable

Fermented with naturally occurring wild yeasts — no inoculation, no control. Just the coffee, the climate, and whatever is in the air. Complex, sometimes funky, always alive.

Process: Wild yeast fermentation · Character: Complex, expressive, spontaneous

🍯 Drawn to naturally fermented coffees? Explore Geisha do Brasil — Danilo Barbosa — a honey processed Geisha where natural fermentation shapes every layer of sweetness and complexity.

🧫 03 — Controlled Yeast Fermentation · Precision & Intention

Inoculated with a selected, controlled yeast strain — the same approach used in winemaking and craft brewing. Consistent, layered, and designed to amplify specific flavour compounds in the coffee.

Process: Controlled yeast inoculation · Character: Structured, fruit-forward, intentional

🍺 Fascinated by controlled fermentation? Meet HOP HOUR — Brasil, Catuai Amarelo by Danilo Barbosa — co-fermented with IPA yeast for 36 hours, delivering tropical fruit and hop-forward citrus in every cup.

🧪 04 — Lactobacillus Fermentation · Science at the Extreme

Fermented with lactobacillus — the same bacteria behind yoghurt, kimchi, and sourdough. Lactic acid fermentation that transforms the coffee's acidity, texture, and depth in ways that challenge every expectation of what coffee can taste like.

Process: Lactobacillus inoculation · Character: Bright acidity, deep complexity, extraordinary texture

🔬 Already obsessed with lactobacillus fermentation? Meet METACAFEÍNA — Castillo 720 by Diego Bermudez — fermented for 720 hours, finished with thermal shock, and used by a World Brewers Cup finalist. A standalone collector's tin for the truly curious.

The Kit

  • 4 coffees × 100g, each in a SOLO Brewing collector's can
  • Limited to 280 kits worldwide
  • All coffees sourced through The Fermentation Project by James Hoffmann
  • Whole beans, roasted to order — ships mid-September 2026
  • Designed for the global cupping event — 3rd October 2026
  • Perfect for filter brewing: V60, Aeropress, Chemex, batch brew

This is not just a coffee kit. It is an invitation to be part of something bigger — a global conversation about fermentation, flavour, and the future of specialty coffee.

products.title: UVA Morangueira – Grapes – Coffee 200g
products.body_html:
Shipping normally at thursdays, as it will be roasted at tuesdays! Join us in our roasting sessions at our coffee shop 

Are you ready to be wowed ?

How often are you suprised with coffee? This is it! This Coffee was infused with natural grapes from colombia, embedding it with fruity aroma that is just not natural in coffees! This is a roller coaster of flavors, deep into this coffee you will find orange blossom, star anise, white flowers and soo much more! This will get your sweet tooth covered, with full on grape that will resemble candy!

A true masterpiece from our friends at Forest and Brayan Avelar, this is an amazing coffee with a high complexity ready to be discovered!

COUNTRY: COLOMBIA, ACEVEDO

FARM: LAS PALMAS

VARIETAL: CASTILLO, CATURRA AND COLOMBIA

ALTITUDE : 1.400-1600 M.A.S.L.

PROCESS : CO-FERMENTED WITH GRAPES

SENSORY NOTES : GRAPES, GRAPES AND MORE GRAPES. SOME FLOWERS BUT MOSTLY GRAPES

FROM THE PRODUCER:

HISTORY: 
Brayan, a proud native of Acevedo, Huila, Colombia, is here to spill the beans on his coffee-filled tale. Nestled in the heart of San Adolfo, a bustling coffee farm, Brayan’s roots run deep in this caffeine-rich soil. It’s like the land itself whispered its secrets to him, shaping his destiny. From a young age, Brayan soaked up coffee wisdom like a sponge, thanks to his pops’ after-school lessons. Little did he know, those coffee chats would ignite a fire within him. Now, alongside 60 like-minded souls (including his own kin), Brayan’s on a quest to share their prized coffee cherries with the world. It’s no easy feat, but they’re up for the challenge. And that’s where the magic happens – with a little help from Forest and the Ancla processing facility, Brayan’s beans get the royal treatment, resulting in flavor profiles that’ll knock your socks off. His dream? Simple yet mighty: to spread the rich, bold taste of San Adolfo Huila’s finest brews far and wide. So keep those mugs ready, folks – Brayan’s brewing up something special!

PROCESS DESCRIPTION: 
The journey of Juicy Grape coffee begins with a carefully crafted blend of Caturra, Castillo, and Colombia varieties. These cherries arrive from the Huila region, produced by Brayan Alvear, highlighting the innovative co-fermentation with fruits that defines its unique profile. The cherries undergo a 24-hour pre-fermentation in plastic bags, followed by 24 hours of fermentation in cherry. After depulpation, the beans are co-fermented anaerobically for 5 days with dehydrated grapes, allowing the coffee to absorb rich, fruity flavors. The beans are then dried mechanically over 10 days, ensuring consistent moisture levels, before a final stabilization period of 5 days. This meticulous process results in a coffee with flavor notes of brown spice, caramel, brown sugar, grape, and red grape.
